research.title: Multiply and Divide Fractions — Prealgebra 2e §4.2, Find Reciprocals
research.retrieved: Official HTML Find Reciprocals definition, nonzero restriction, sign reasoning, whole-number example and comparison with opposites; current licence footer.
research.adopted: Product-one is the defining relationship. State zero exception, write whole numbers over one, and keep reciprocal separate from opposite.
research.rejected: No automatic flip rule for zero, no claim reciprocal always increases magnitude, no general fraction-division algorithm imported as a prerequisite.
research.usageRestrictions: Current page states CC BY-NC-SA and separate AI/commercial permission restrictions. Concept comparison of mathematical facts only; no protected text, exercise, media or code reused.

research.title: Reciprocals
research.organisation: Ximera, Ohio State-hosted CSCC Mathematics PreCalculus
research.retrieved: Official HTML reciprocal/zero, size and sign subsections; CC BY-NC-SA4.0 shown. No embedded graph/video review claimed.
research.adopted: Zero cannot be inverted into a valid fraction; one is its own reciprocal; both negative members can multiply to positive one.
research.rejected: Do not import limits, asymptotes or reciprocal functions. Source size paragraph contains a wording slip calling the opposite-sign A/A form value1; rely on direct arithmetic giving−1, not that sentence.
research.usageRestrictions: Page states CC BY-NC-SA4.0. No external text/diagram/code copied; own strip model.
